chapter: Joining Earl Hines and the Grand Terrace
title: Battle of the bands with Chick Webb at the Savoy; Tuskegee
summary: The Hines band always lost to Webb at his home ballroom.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: The Savoy, Chick Webb was the house band there?

Right. We'd lose all the time. In fact, Duke Ellington even lost. Chick Webb, boy, he had a tough band, and tough arrangements. Oh, man. Boy, he had a whole band -- our bandstand would be jumping. And we wouldn't even be playing.
Yeah, opposite. One like over here, and we'd be at this end of the hall. Two bandstands.
How did those contests get started?
It became a commercial thing, I know, the Battle of the Bands.
And who was the judge? The crowd?
The crowd, yeah. You know, naturally see, that was Chick Webb's home.
Yeah. Did Hines band play any other battles? With other bands?
We'd play against other bands, but it
wasn't a battle. Like some places we'd play we'd have help, like when we played Tuskegee, Alabama, that's where I first met Hawk, "Tuxedo Junction" Hawk.
Yeah, Erskine Hawkins. He was a school band.
